Procurement has two gating items before we can engage legal and finalize PO: a formal price-lock / ceiling for the full 4-year term, and an annual uplift cap (we'd prefer <=6% per year). Subject: Fwd: Crestline procurement — exec approval requested for price lock + uplift cap (DL-9283)

Marissa / Markus — escalating Crestline. Key facts:
- Customer: Crestline Health (large regional health system)
- Deal: 4-year committed term, $4.32M total committed; Year 1 MRR ~$90k
- Request: explicit 4-year price lock (no increases above ceiling), uplift cap requested <=6% per annum, renewal-protection language to prevent automatic re-benchmarking that could trigger higher unit prices
- Timing: Crestline needs sign-off by 2027-10-22 to make their FY procurement window

Why this needs exec: our standard T&C allows annual pricing adjustments tied to costs; the customer is asking for a flat ceiling and caps that would limit that flexibility. Deal Desk can approve up to 3-year locks at standard rates, but this is a 4-year lock + uplift cap request. We estimate marginal incremental revenue risk if we lock below indexation — but the stability should materially increase probability of close and expansion.

Attachments: Crestline_PO_Form.docx (from customer). I also attached the original proposal.

Proposed compromise we could offer pending exec guidance:
- 4-year ceiling on base unit price (no increases beyond this ceiling)
- Uplift cap 5% per annum (company to propose 5% vs customer 6%)
- Renewal protection: require 90-day advance notice and mutual re-negotiation window; automatic renewals keep previous year's pricing unless both parties agree

Open to your guidance. I'll coordinate legal redlines once we have approval.

Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc:
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Crestline procurement — exec approval requested for price lock + uplift cap (DL-9283)

Ben / Markus — after reviewing the numbers and the strategic value, I approve escalation with the following negotiated constraints:

1) Price lock: Redwood will commit to a firm ceiling on the base per-unit price for the full 48-month term (no increases above the ceiling regardless of cost indices).
2) Uplift cap: limit annual uplift to 5% maximum; this will apply only to contracted consumption tiers and not to usage that exceeds the agreed tiers (we'll keep overage pricing separate).
3) Renewal protection: include a clause that prevents unilateral re-definition of billing units for the first renewal period; automatic renewal keeps prior-year pricing unless both parties sign a mutually agreed amendment within a 90-day notice window.
4) Strategic carve-outs: Redwood reserves the right to apply separate surcharges for any material changes in regulatory compliance costs or mandatory cloud provider pass-throughs beyond our control — such surcharges must be communicated 120 days in advance and limited to actual cost delta.

Conditions: Legal to prepare redline with those bullets and include a 10% discount floor for Year 1 (as in the proposal). Finance to model downside sensitivity to a 2%/yr inflation in unit costs and confirm margin coverage. This approval is time-limited: if we do not receive signed PO by 2027-10-29, the approval expires and Deal Desk needs to re-run.

I'll attach draft redline language for Legal to pickup. Ben, please loop in Rachel Park on the legal side and ask Crestline to confirm their purchase order timeline.

Marissa Cole

Emily — looping back with approved language from Redwood leadership. Thank you for the quick turn. Summary of agreed points (as approved by Redwood execs):

- 4-year firm ceiling on base unit price (no increases above that ceiling for the 48-month term).
- Annual uplift cap: 5% per annum applied to contracted tiers (Crestline requested 6%; Redwood approved 5% as a commercial concession).
- Renewal protection: automatic renewal will preserve prior-year pricing unless both parties mutually agree to an amendment within a 90-day notice window.
- Carve-outs: regulatory/cloud pass-throughs allowed with 120-day notice, limited to actual cost deltas.
- Finance/legal conditions: 10% discount floor in Year 1 remains; final redlines to be executed by both parties.
